mainTopic: בר קפרא's mistake about איסור כולל and בת אחת cases, the זר serving on שבת, and the משנה of brides accidentally switched at the חופה.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining בר קפרא's mistake. רבי taught him that, according to רבי שמעון, a person is exempt from a second prohibition in איסור כולל cases. בר קפרא then mixed in the case of a זר who ate a מליקה bird, which is a בת אחת case, and wrongly decided that every case carried an exemption. A ברייתא about a זר serving on שבת leaves out the מליקה case, which shows that even רבי שמעון holds a person liable twice in a בת אחת case, so בר קפרא is refuted. The גמרא then asks which service the זר in that ברייתא did on שבת. רב אחא בר יעקב answers that it was the כהן גדול's bull. רב אשי answers that the ברייתא only counts prohibitions, which matters for burial among the completely wicked. A new משנה follows about two brides switched at the חופה, listing the prohibitions involved and what happens to the women afterward. The גמרא then shows from the משנה itself that the switch happened by accident (הוּחְלְפוּ), as רב יהודה said.

steps.title: What רבי really taught, and how בר קפרא added a case
steps.stepSummary: רבי taught בר קפרא the איסור כולל cases according to רבי שמעון. בר קפרא then added the case of a זר who ate a מליקה bird and found it could only be a 'both at once' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי taught him the rule of an inclusive prohibition, following רבי שמעון. בר קפרא also saw the case of a non-priest who ate a pinched bird. Since it looked similar, he mixed it in with the others. When he looked into it, he saw that this case can only happen with both prohibitions starting at the same moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining how בר קפרא's mistaken report came about. רבי taught him one thing, and בר קפרא added a similar-looking case on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What רבי actually taught was the איסור כולל cases, according to רבי שמעון's view. The מליקה case is different, because the bird becomes forbidden as קדשים and as נבלה at the same moment it is pinched. So it can only be a בת אחת case. בר קפרא grouped it with the others anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'inclusive prohibition': a second prohibition that takes hold because it now covers more people or things
A bird offering killed by pinching its neck with the fingernail
All at once: both prohibitions start at the same moment

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of cases. In an איסור כולל case, one prohibition comes first and the second one joins later. In a בת אחת case, both start at the same instant.

phrases.english: And he taught him the case of an inclusive prohibition,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי, teaching בר קפרא. This continues רבי חייא's explanation from just before.

phrases.english: and that was according to Rabbi Shimon.
And bar Kappara saw the case of a non-priest who ate a pinched bird,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the letter in round brackets. The meaning is the same either way.

phrases.english: and since it resembled those cases,
he mixed it in together with them,
and he examined it,
and found that it could only happen all at once.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיסּוּר כּוֹלֵל אַתְנְיֵיהּ, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי חייא's explanation, from before this section, of how בר קפרא came to misreport רבי's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי taught only the איסור כולל exemption according to רבי שמעון. The מליקה case, which is a בת אחת case, was added by בר קפרא.

steps.title: בר קפרא's mistaken reasoning
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא reasoned that since the מליקה case is 'all at once', the others must be too. And since the others are exempt, all of them must be exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought: since this case is all at once, that case is also all at once. And since those cases are exempt, these cases are also exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two-part chain of reasoning that led בר קפרא to his wrong conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First he took the 'all at once' feature of the מליקה case and applied it to the other cases. Then he took the exemption of the other cases and applied it to the מליקה case. The result was a mistaken rule that a person is exempt even when two prohibitions start together. He was not lying, just confused.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that בר קפרא's claim came from an honest mistake in grouping cases together, not from anything רבי actually said.

phrases.english: And he reasoned: since this one is all at once,
that one is also all at once.
And since those are taught as exempt,
these are also taught as exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the explanation by showing the logical leap בר קפרא made after grouping the cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בר קפרא wrongly concluded that every case, including the בת אחת cases, carries an exemption from the second prohibition.

steps.title: A ברייתא where רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון argue, with the מליקה case left out
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a מחלוקת about a זר serving on שבת and a בעל מום serving while טמא. It does not mention the מליקה case.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: A non-priest who did the Temple service on שבת, and a blemished priest who served while impure. רבי יוסי says he is liable for each prohibition: being a non-priest, שבת, being blemished, and impurity. רבי שמעון says he is liable only for being a non-priest and for being blemished. Yet the מליקה case was left out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge בר קפרא. It points out that the מליקה case is missing from this מחלוקת, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי makes a person liable for every prohibition, even in איסור כולל cases. רבי שמעון exempts the second prohibition in those cases. The key point is the silence: the ברייתא does not list the מליקה case. That gap is what the גמרא will use against בר קפרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Being a non-priest who does the Temple service
A כהן with a physical blemish, who may not serve

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
A non-priest who did the service on Shabbat,
and a blemished priest who served while impure,

phrases.aramaic: יֵשׁ כָּאן מִשּׁוּם זָרוּת, וּמִשּׁוּם שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: there is liability here for being a non-priest, and for Shabbat,
and for being blemished, and for impurity,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
Rabbi Shimon says:
There is liability here only for being a non-priest
and for being blemished, nothing more.
Yet the pinched bird case he left out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining בר קפרא's mistake to actively challenging his claim from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר קפרא's claim that there is an exemption even in the זר שאכל מליקה case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists the cases the תנאים argue about but leaves out מליקה. That suggests the מליקה case follows a different rule.

steps.title: Whose view explains leaving out the מליקה case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the omission reflects. It shows that it cannot be about רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom did he leave it out? If you say according to רבי יוסי: he already makes a person liable twice even with an inclusive prohibition. Do we even need to say so when both prohibitions start at once?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא the missing case teaches us about. It first rules out רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי makes a person liable twice even in the weaker איסור כולל cases. So of course he would make a person liable in a בת אחת case. Leaving out מליקה would teach us nothing new about him, so the omission must be teaching about someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Now (that), introducing an 'all the more so' argument
Is it even necessary to say?

phrases.english: According to whom did he leave it out?
If you say it is according to Rabbi Yosei,
now, if Rabbi Yosei, with an inclusive prohibition,
makes him liable for two,
is it even necessary to say so with a prohibition that comes all at once?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts working out what the omission noticed in the ברייתא actually proves.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view does leaving out the מליקה case teach us about?

steps.title: The omission reflects רבי שמעון: he makes a person liable in a בת אחת case
steps.stepSummary: The omission must be according to רבי שמעון. So he exempts only in איסור כולל cases, and makes a person liable when both prohibitions come at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it according to רבי שמעון? So it is only with an inclusive prohibition that he exempts. But with a prohibition that comes all at once, he makes a person liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the מליקה case was left out of רבי שמעון's exemptions because he agrees there is liability for both prohibitions there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's exemption is limited to the איסור כולל cases. In a בת אחת case like מליקה, even he holds the person liable twice. That is the opposite of what בר קפרא claimed.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון exempts only in איסור כולל cases. When two prohibitions start at the same moment (בת אחת), he agrees the person is liable for both.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it according to Rabbi Shimon?
So it is with an inclusive prohibition that he exempts,
but with a prohibition that comes all at once, one is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from the previous step by pointing to רבי שמעון.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The omission follows רבי שמעון, who holds a person liable twice in a בת אחת case.

steps.title: בר קפרא is fully refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares בר קפרא's position conclusively refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of בר קפרא is a full refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion by stating that בר קפרא's claim has been knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא said there is an exemption even in a בת אחת case. The ברייתא shows that even רבי שמעון makes a person liable in such a case. So no one holds בר קפרא's view, and it is rejected.
steps.whatToRemember: בר קפרא's claim of an exemption in בת אחת cases is rejected. The exemption applies only to איסור כולל cases, and only according to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: The refutation of bar Kappara is a conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the final outcome of the challenge built in the previous steps.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: בר קפרא's position is rejected. Both רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון make a person liable twice when two prohibitions start at the same moment.

steps.title: Which service did the non-priest do on Shabbat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which עבודה the ברייתא's זר did on שבת. It rules out שחיטה and קבלה/הולכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A non-priest who served on שבת: with what? If with slaughtering, slaughtering by a non-priest is valid. If with receiving and carrying the blood, that is just moving things around.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's case of a זר serving on שבת and asks which service he did. It starts crossing off options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For two prohibitions, the act must be both forbidden to a זר and a real מלאכה on שבת. שחיטה is a מלאכה, but a זר is allowed to do it. קבלה and הולכה are forbidden to a זר, but they are only carrying, not a real מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Receiving the blood in a vessel and carrying it to the מזבח
Moving or carrying an object; here, not a full מלאכה

phrases.english: A non-priest who served on Shabbat: with what [service]?
If with slaughtering,
slaughtering by a non-priest is valid.
And if with receiving and carrying [the blood],
that is merely moving things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After closing the בר קפרא discussion, the גמרא returns to clarify a case inside the ברייתא from step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which עבודה makes a זר break both שבת and the זר prohibition.

steps.title: Burning on the altar runs into רבי יוסי's view
steps.stepSummary: הקטרה is a problem because רבי יוסי holds that lighting a fire on שבת is only a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did the burning on the altar, didn't רבי יוסי say that kindling was singled out as just a prohibition?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the last option, burning on the מזבח. It finds a problem with it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הקטרה is both forbidden to a זר and an act of lighting fire. But רבי יוסי says הבערה on שבת is only a plain לאו, not like the other מלאכות. So it is hard to count it as a full second violation.

keyTerms.meaning: Burning the parts of a קרבן on the מזבח
A plain negative prohibition, less severe than the other מלאכות

phrases.english: If with burning [on the altar],
but didn't Rabbi Yosei say
kindling was singled out as [just] a prohibition?
phrases.notes: He means lighting a fire on שבת is set apart from the other מלאכות and is only a plain לאו.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַבְעָרָה לְלָאו יָצָאתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues crossing off options, now ruling out the last one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The option that the זר's service was הקטרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי יוסי, הבערה is only a לאו, so it would not count as a full שבת violation on top of the זר prohibition.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: the כהן גדול's bull
steps.stepSummary: The case is the שחיטה of the כהן גדול's bull on יום כיפור, following the view that a זר may not slaughter it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: it is the slaughtering of the High Priest's bull, following the one who says a non-priest may not slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב finds a case that works: a special שחיטה that a זר may not do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a זר may do שחיטה. But one opinion holds the כהן גדול's bull on יום כיפור must be slaughtered by him alone. Then the זר breaks the זר prohibition, and שחיטה is also a full מלאכה on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull the כהן גדול brings on יום כיפור

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
With the slaughtering of the High Priest's bull,
phrases.notes: The bull brought on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: and according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: שְׁחִיטַת פָּרוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּזָר פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: the slaughtering of the High Priest's bull by a non-priest is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem left by steps 7 and 8 by naming a case that works.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a special situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No עבודה could make a זר break both prohibitions.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שחיטה of the כהן גדול's bull is forbidden to a זר and is also a full מלאכה on שבת.

steps.title: Why say a non-priest? Even a regular priest is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: If the case is the כהן גדול's bull, a כהן הדיוט is also forbidden. So why does the ברייתא say זר?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why specifically a non-priest? Even a regular priest too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא's answer from the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only the כהן גדול may slaughter his bull, then a regular כהן doing it is just as forbidden. Picking out a זר seems too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular כהן, not the כהן גדול

phrases.english: If so, why specifically a non-priest?
Even a regular priest as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אחא בר יעקב's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's case of the כהן גדול's bull
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In that case a regular כהן is also forbidden, so the ברייתא should not have limited it to a זר.

steps.title: 'Non-priest' means an outsider relative to the High Priest
steps.stepSummary: זר here means anyone who is an outsider compared to the כהן גדול, including a regular כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means one who is a 'stranger' compared to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording problem by reading the word זר more broadly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word זר means an outsider. For this עבודה, anyone other than the כהן גדול is an outsider, even a regular כהן. So the ברייתא's wording includes him.

keyTerms.meaning: An outsider compared to him, here the כהן גדול

phrases.english: It means one who is a stranger in relation to him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the כהן גדול, so for this service even a regular כהן counts as an outsider.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב אחא's answer against step 10.
steps.terutzMaskana: זר means anyone who is an outsider to this עבודה, including a regular כהן.

steps.title: רב אשי: the ברייתא is only listing prohibitions
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the ברייתא is not counting חטאות or לאוין. It just lists prohibitions, so even הקטרה works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: is the ברייתא teaching sin-offerings, or teaching לאוין? Rather, it is just counting prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues that the problem in step 8 was never a real problem, so רב אחא's special case is not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with הקטרה was that, for רבי יוסי, הבערה is only a לאו. רב אשי says the ברייתא is not ranking how severe each violation is. It only lists which prohibitions were broken, and הבערה still counts as one.

keyTerms.meaning: Just prohibitions, without ranking their severity

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not arguing with רבי יוסי about הבערה. He agrees it is only a לאו. He says that doesn't matter, because the ברייתא is only counting prohibitions.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi strongly objected to this:
Is it teaching sin-offerings,
or is it teaching negative prohibitions?!
Rather, it is merely counting prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the problem from step 8 that made רב אחא's answer necessary.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The problem against הקטרה in step 8, and so the need for רב אחא בר יעקב's answer
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the ברייתא was counting penalties, when it only lists prohibitions.

steps.title: What difference does counting prohibitions make?
steps.stepSummary: If no extra penalty follows, why does it matter how many prohibitions he broke?
steps.simpleTranslation: What practical difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a bare count of prohibitions matters at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רב אשי says the list doesn't change חטאות or punishments, the count seems to have no effect. The גמרא wants a practical result.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: For what does it make a difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about רב אשי's idea of 'just counting prohibitions'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical effect of counting more prohibitions.

steps.title: It matters for burial among the completely wicked
steps.stepSummary: The count decides whether he is buried among the completely wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: To bury him among the completely wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical difference: where the person is buried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with no extra קרבן or punishment, each prohibition adds to how wicked the person is. That affects which section of the cemetery he is buried in.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's זר on שבת is explained two ways. רב אחא בר יעקב says it is the כהן גדול's bull. רב אשי says even הקטרה works, because the list only counts prohibitions, and that count matters for burial among the completely wicked.

phrases.english: To bury him among the completely wicked.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Counting prohibitions decides whether the person is buried among the completely wicked.

steps.title: Two brides switched at the wedding canopy
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if two betrothed women were switched at the חופה, the men are liable for אשת איש, and also for אשת אח, אחות אשה, or נדה when those apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two men were each מקדש a woman. When they entered the חופה, each man ended up with the other's wife. They are liable for אשת איש. If the men were brothers, they are also liable for אשת אח. If the women were sisters, they are also liable for marrying a woman and her sister. If the women were נדות, they are also liable for נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It describes two couples whose brides were switched at the חופה, and it lists every prohibition the men could be breaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין alone already makes a woman forbidden to every other man as an אשת איש. So the moment each man lives with the other's wife, he breaks that prohibition. Each extra detail (brothers, sisters, נדה) piles on another separate prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: They betrothed (did קידושין), which already makes the woman a married woman in הלכה
The wedding canopy, the second stage of marriage
They switched (an active verb, as if done on purpose)
A married woman, forbidden to all other men
Taking a woman together with her sister

steps.confusionAlert: Even though they had only reached קידושין and not yet the חופה, the women already count as fully married for the איסור of אשת איש.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Two men who betrothed two women,
and at the time they entered the wedding canopy
they switched this one's wife to that one
and that one's wife to this one

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אֵלּוּ חַיָּיבִין מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ.
phrases.english: these are liable for a married woman.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיוּ אַחִין — מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָח.
phrases.english: And if they were brothers, also for a brother's wife.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיוּ אֲחָיוֹת — מִשּׁוּם ״אִשָּׁה אֶל אֲחוֹתָהּ״.
phrases.english: And if the women were sisters, also for 'a woman with her sister'.
phrases.notes: This is quoting the פסוק in ויקרא 18:18.

phrases.english: And if they were menstruating, also for a menstruating woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the earlier discussion about the כהן גדול and counting prohibitions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Switched brides make the men liable for אשת איש, plus אשת אח, אחות אשה, and נדה where relevant.

steps.title: What happens to the women afterward
steps.stepSummary: The women are separated from their husbands for three months in case they became pregnant. Minors who cannot bear children go back at once, and כהנות become disqualified from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We keep the women away from their husbands for three months, in case they became pregnant. If they were young girls who cannot have children, we send them back right away. If they were daughters of כהנים, they can no longer eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the practical results for the women after the switch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three-month wait makes it possible to tell whose baby it is if one is born. Girls too young to have children don't need that wait, so they return immediately. The forbidden relations also take away a כהן's daughter's right to eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: We separate (the women from their husbands)
The holy portion of produce that only כהנים and their households may eat

phrases.english: And we separate them for three months,
in case they are pregnant.
And if they were minors
who are not able to give birth,
we return them immediately.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיוּ כֹּהֲנוֹת, נִפְסְלוּ מִן הַתְּרוּמָה.
phrases.english: And if they were daughters of priests, they are disqualified from teruma.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with the follow-up rules for the women.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three-month separation, immediate return for minors who cannot bear children, and loss of תרומה for כהנות.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that minors go back immediately becomes the basis for an attempted proof later in the גמרא.

steps.title: Would the משנה describe such wicked people?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the word הֶחְלִיפוּ: would the משנה really deal with men who deliberately swapped wives?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'they switched.' Are we really talking about wicked people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges the wording of the משנה. 'They switched' sounds like the men did it on purpose, and that seems unlikely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The active verb suggests a deliberate swap of wives, which would be outrageous behavior. The משנה normally doesn't build its cases around wicked people, so the wording looks wrong.

phrases.english: GEMARA: 'They switched.'
Are we dealing with wicked people?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the משנה's verb from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word הֶחְלִיפוּ in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An active 'they switched' implies a deliberate wife swap, and it is unlikely the משנה is describing such wicked people.

steps.title: Sin-offerings don't fit an intentional act
steps.stepSummary: A second attack: רבי חייא counted sixteen חטאות in this case, but a קרבן is only brought for an accidental sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, רבי חייא taught: 'There are sixteen sin-offerings here.' But if they did it on purpose, is there any קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger problem with reading the משנה as a deliberate switch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is only brought for a sin done by mistake (שוגג). רבי חייא counted sixteen חטאות here, four for each of the four people, so he must have understood the act as accidental. That contradicts the active 'they switched.'

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which Rabbi Ḥiyya taught:
'There are sixteen sin-offerings here.'
phrases.notes: Four people, and each one broke four prohibitions, so 4 × 4 = 16.

phrases.english: If it was intentional, is there an offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the one in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading הֶחְלִיפוּ as a deliberate act
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חייא counts sin-offerings, and those are only brought for unintentional sins, so the case must be accidental.

steps.title: Read it as 'they were switched'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה fixes the wording of the משנה to הוּחְלְפוּ, so the switch happened by accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Read the משנה as 'they were switched.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers both problems by changing one word in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the passive form, nobody chose to swap anything. The women got mixed up by mistake. That removes the 'wicked people' problem and explains why sin-offerings apply.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is about an accidental mix-up, not a deliberate swap. That is why רבי חייא can count sixteen חטאות.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Teach: 'they were switched.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both objections from steps 17 and 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'הֶחְלִיפוּ' meant the men deliberately swapped wives.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read 'הוּחְלְפוּ': the women were switched by accident, so the act was שוגג.

steps.title: Support from the rule about minors
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to support רב יהודה: the משנה returns minors to their husbands immediately, and that would not be allowed if the act had been deliberate.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, because the end of the משנה teaches: If they were minors who cannot give birth, we return them immediately. If it was on purpose, would that be allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from the end of the משנה that the case was an accident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife who willingly sinned with another man becomes forbidden to her husband. Since the משנה sends the minors straight back, the act must not have been willing on their part, which fits an accidental switch.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of the משנה

phrases.english: This too stands to reason,
since the last clause teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיוּ קְטַנּוֹת שֶׁאֵינָן רְאוּיוֹת לֵילֵד —
phrases.english: If they were minors not able to give birth,
we return them immediately.
And if it was intentional, would she be permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב יהודה's reading in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's reading הוּחְלְפוּ (an accidental switch)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: minors are returned to their husbands immediately.

steps.title: Seducing a minor counts as אונס
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: even a deliberate act with a minor counts as אונס, and a woman who was forced stays permitted to an ישראל husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: seducing a minor counts as rape, and a woman who was raped is permitted to an ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 20 and shows that the minors' rule does not prove the act was accidental.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor's agreement means nothing in הלכה, so even if she was seduced, it counts as אונס. A woman who suffered אונס is not forbidden to an ישראל husband. So minors would go back right away even if the switch was deliberate, and the proof falls away, though רב יהודה's reading still stands on its own.
steps.confusionAlert: This only rejects the extra proof. It does not cancel רב יהודה's reading הוּחְלְפוּ, which the objections in steps 17 and 18 still support.

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
the seduction of a minor counts as rape,
and after rape she is permitted to an Israelite.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: פִּיתּוּי קְטַנָּה אוֹנֶס נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the supporting proof from step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the supporting proof from the minors' rule, not רב יהודה's reading itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The minors' immediate return can be explained even for a deliberate act, because seducing a minor counts as אונס, and אונס does not forbid her to an ישראל husband.

steps.title: A new proof from the three-month separation
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the women are separated for three months only because they might be pregnant. That means they are permitted to their husbands afterward, which could not be true if they had sinned deliberately. So the switch must have been accidental.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, prove it from what the משנה teaches: 'We separate them for three months, because perhaps they are pregnant.' This implies that if they are not pregnant, they are permitted to their husbands. If they had acted deliberately, would they be permitted? So isn't this a proof that they were switched by accident?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the rejected proof about the minors and tries a new proof for רב יהודה from a different line of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason the משנה gives for keeping the women away from their husbands is a possible pregnancy. That suggests that if there is no pregnancy, nothing else stops them from going back. A grown woman who knowingly sinned with another man becomes forbidden to her husband permanently. So the משנה must be talking about an accidental switch, just as רב יהודה said with הוּחְלְפוּ.

keyTerms.meaning: We separate (the wives from their husbands)
But if not (introduces an inference from the משנה's wording)

steps.confusionAlert: This proof is stronger than the one in step 20. That proof was about minors, and even a deliberate act with a minor counts as אונס. Here the משנה is talking about adult women, so the אונס answer does not work.
steps.whyThisMatters: It firmly fixes the reading of the משנה as הוּחְלְפוּ. That also answers both attacks in steps 17-18, including רבי חייא's sixteen חטאות, since a חטאת is brought only for an accidental sin.

phrases.english: Rather, prove it from what it teaches:
We separate them for three months
because perhaps they are pregnant.
This implies that if they are not pregnant, they are permitted,
and if it was deliberate, would it be permitted?
So isn't it so? Learn from this that they were switched by accident.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof rejected in step 21 with a new proof for the same claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's reading הוּחְלְפוּ: the switch was accidental.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's line that the women are separated for three months because they might be pregnant. This implies they are permitted to their husbands afterward, which would be impossible if the act was deliberate.

steps.title: The proof is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: learn from here that the משנה means the wives were switched by accident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Indeed, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the proof from step 22 and closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one pushes back this time, so the reading הוּחְלְפוּ stands. The משנה is about an accidental switch. That fits both the women going back to their husbands and the חטאות brought for the sin.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it: the גמרא's way of accepting a proof

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's case is an accidental switch (הוּחְלְפוּ), as רב יהודה said. Two things prove it. The adult wives may go back to their husbands after three months if they are not pregnant. And חטאות are brought only for accidental sins.

phrases.english: Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof given in step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה should be read as הוּחְלְפוּ: the wives were switched by accident.
